reasons.rubric: Predicate is a simple threshold and the verifier over-collects, but the issuer is an unwilling platform (zkTLS) and the committees rarely care, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Courier access passes are real, but a platform stat does not establish identity at the door and zkTLS scraping of a driver app is fragile and likely against terms.
reasons.coherence: The idea itself admits that the issuer did not agree, the verifier does not care, and identity needs a separate check, which undercuts the benefit.
reasons.novelty: Courier access to buildings and platform-stat zkTLS are not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings are generic over-collection patterns about age scans and bank KYC; the idea reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: No retention duty is apparent; committees keep screenshots by habit.
reasons.linkability: A threshold proof from a session replay reveals little and is not linkable beyond the account.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform explicitly did not agree to issue and may forbid session replay.
reasons.no_wallet: Couriers have phones, but the verifying building office has no verification infrastructure or incentive.

reasons.rubric: A bounded yes/no from a hospital with high frequency, but needs a new real-time clinic attestation and the centre has some reporting duty, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: School return after illness is a real recurring moment and a 'may attend from date A' note is sufficient for staff, but clinics do not issue digital status credentials today.
reasons.coherence: The predicate, issuer and verifier fit well, though the child-held wallet issue and the reporting duty are acknowledged.
reasons.novelty: Child health clearance for school return is not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings are generic record-minimisation points about policy versus technical limits; the idea is the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: The centre may need to report notifiable diseases, but it can report without holding the clinic certificate itself, so the unknown remains.
reasons.linkability: Single-use short window claim with a clinic issuer is low risk, though issuer phone-home is unspecified.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Paediatric clinics have little incentive or tooling to issue digital attestations.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents act for the child and could hold the credential on a phone, so this is workable but awkward.

reasons.rubric: A yes/no health status is simple, but frequency is low and the issuer would need real-time attestation, so a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Pre-boarding health checks existed in Taiwan, but the need is low-frequency and a clearance of notifiable infection is not a standard clinic product.
reasons.coherence: A short-lived status and a one-time boarding desk fit, though the idea concedes the hospital cannot issue it in real time.
reasons.novelty: Travel boarding health clearance is not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The borrowing of yes/no proof and no-copy guidance is generic and the idea reads the same without it.
reasons.retention_law: The idea itself says port or quarantine rules may require records, and Taiwanese law is unknown to me here.
reasons.linkability: A short-window boolean limits linkability if the issuer does not see use.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals do not issue real-time status credentials and have no demand to start.
reasons.no_wallet: Travellers carry phones, but the boarding desk would need verifier tooling.

reasons.rubric: A non-membership boolean from a government issuer exists, but the legally mandated check may require the employer to query directly, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Employers hiring staff for children's settings really do check, but a holder-presented proof may not satisfy the legal check and freshness is a real gap.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit well and the idea honestly names the legal route and freshness problems.
reasons.novelty: Criminal-record and rental are on the known list, so this is a narrower predicate and new issuer on a close moment.
reasons.provenance: The borrowed bundling and no-tracking points loosely mirror the good-conduct certificate issue but the idea stands without them.
reasons.retention_law: Employers appear obliged to query official lists directly, which may block the benefit; the exact rule is unknown to me.
reasons.linkability: A non-membership proof from a government source can be unlinkable if designed with care.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The police administration is a plausible issuer but has no current mechanism for narrow attestations.
reasons.no_wallet: Applicants are adults with phones and the TW wallet is plausible.

reasons.rubric: A current-employment boolean with a revocable employer signature, but fragmented employer issuers and a possible direct insurance query make it a design problem.
reasons.validity: Duplicate labour-insurance enrolment on side jobs is real, but the predicate may not match what the platform legally needs and the employer must cooperate.
reasons.coherence: The idea concedes that issuing could tip off the employer and that the platform may query records directly, which undermines the premise.
reasons.novelty: Side-job eligibility and insurance duplication are not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The borrowing about demanding documents without a stated purpose is decorative and the idea reads the same without it.
reasons.retention_law: Whether the platform must keep the employer letter is unknown to me.
reasons.linkability: A revocable status credential implies the issuer can see or infer checking, which creates linkage and tip-off risk.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Employers have no incentive to issue statements that help staff moonlight and may restrict it.
reasons.no_wallet: Workers hold phones but employers lack any credential issuing system.

reasons.rubric: A roll membership boolean from a single issuer, but low frequency and the responder needs the address in an emergency, so a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Priority lists for medical-equipment households are real, but the idea admits dispatch needs location and outages break wallet access.
reasons.coherence: A single roll and a single issuer fit, though the usable window is limited to pre-registration.
reasons.novelty: Disaster relief and medical power dependence are not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The sealed-bid and ID-copy borrowings are unrelated to this setting and decorative.
reasons.retention_law: No clear duty to retain a diagnosis certificate is apparent, but I cannot be sure for emergency services.
reasons.linkability: A membership proof still ties to the account and address at dispatch, so linkage is partly unavoidable.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taipower is a state-owned utility and may be willing, but running a credential service is not its current role.
reasons.no_wallet: Outages and elderly or ill households make wallet access unreliable exactly when needed.

reasons.rubric: A uniqueness nullifier is a one-person-one-claim predicate on a high-frequency promotion, but the telco issuer ecosystem and multi-line holding make it a design problem.
reasons.validity: Coupon abuse with throwaway SIMs is real, but a per-line credential does not give per-person uniqueness unless the telco binds to national ID.
reasons.coherence: The idea honestly flags multi-line, prepaid and incentive gaps that weaken the central claim.
reasons.novelty: Sybil resistance is on the known list for brokerage, but a promotion drop with a telco issuer is a new issuer and moment.
reasons.retention_law: No legal duty to retain the phone number is apparent for a promotion.
reasons.linkability: A per-campaign nullifier avoids cross-service linkage, though the telco could see issuance.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telcos are multiple and have little incentive to issue per-person credentials for coupons.
reasons.no_wallet: Users already hold phones and apps, so wallet delivery is plausible.

reasons.rubric: A narrow non-membership boolean from a government issuer, but low-to-medium frequency and legal checks that may need the fuller record make it a design problem.
reasons.validity: Parents and small operators do ask for 良民證, but the register absence is narrower than what they may legitimately want and covered jobs need an official check.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit, and the idea honestly states the false-comfort and legal-check limits.
reasons.novelty: It is nearly the same as the known criminal-record case and also overlaps with b04-3, so mostly a narrower variant.
reasons.provenance: The retention and deletion-exception borrowings are generic and the idea is unchanged without them.
reasons.retention_law: Covered employers appear obliged to check registries and possibly retain results; the exact scope is unknown to me.
reasons.linkability: A government non-membership proof can be unlinkable if designed carefully.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The police administration or Ministry of Justice has no narrow-attestation product and may resist.
reasons.no_wallet: Candidates are adults with phones but informal parent verifiers lack tooling.
